title: Recommendations for return of secondary genomic findings in observational cohort studies.

verified.what_i_actually_checked: Ran the paper-context tool: Europe PMC flags say not open access, no PMC identifier, hasSuppl=N, hasData=N, no accession numbers in text or text-mined, no NCBI GEO/SRA/BioProject/dbGaP links, and a Zenodo/Dryad search on the DOI returned nothing. Crossref confirms a 25-author, 11-page (2437-2447) article with 131 references and only a text-and-data-mining licence, i.e. a Perspective-style synthesis, with no related-dataset relation recorded.
verified.what_came_from_paper_text_only: The abstract only. Full text is paywalled and not in PubMed Central, so I read no methods or data-availability statement. The abstract describes the article as a synthesis of a 2024 National Heart, Lung and Blood Institute workshop plus literature, offering guidance - it reports no measurements.

a1_downloadable.note: There is no dataset at all. No supplementary files, no accession numbers, no repository deposit, and the article itself is paywalled with no PubMed Central copy. Nothing to download, so A1 fails outright.

a2_label_is_a_column.note: Not assessable and moot: with no data table there is no column, and any label (for example 'should this finding be returned to the participant?') would have to be constructed by hand from policy prose.

a3_inputs_present.note: No input features of any kind. The article contains recommendations and references, not genomic variants, participant records or any machine-readable feature set.

a5_enough_rows.note: Zero rows of data. Row count is null because no file exists to count.

a6_fits_laptop.note: Trivially fits on a laptop because there is nothing to load; this is not a pass in any useful sense.

a7_counts_match_paper.note: No counts are claimed and no files exist, so the check cannot be performed.

a8_label_provenance.note: No label exists. Any target would come from expert committee opinion, i.e. human judgement about policy, not from a physical measurement.

honest_claim_h3: No claim is possible: the article is a policy Perspective with no accompanying data, so no model could be trained or evaluated from it.

plain_idea.one_liner: Use a genomic variant's properties to predict whether experts would return it to a research participant as a secondary finding.
plain_idea.train_on: The project I considered would need one row per gene-variant pair with its evidence attributes (disease severity, how actionable the condition is, how confident the pathogenicity call is). This paper supplies none of these; verified example count is zero.
plain_idea.predict: Whether a finding is classified as returnable to a cohort participant. The true answer would come from expert panel decisions such as the American College of Medical Genetics and Genomics (ACMG) actionable gene list, which are human judgements rather than lab measurements.
plain_idea.why_worthwhile: Biobanks and cohort studies must triage millions of incidental genomic findings, so automating the triage would save curator time; but this particular article provides only narrative recommendations, so it cannot support that project.

ml_idea: None viable from this article. The nearest idea - predicting whether a secondary genomic finding should be returned to a participant - would have to be built entirely from external resources (the ACMG secondary findings gene list, ClinVar pathogenicity records, ClinGen actionability scores), none of which this paper contributes or links to.

effort.compute_note: No compute estimates are meaningful because no data file exists; all fields left null rather than guessed.
effort.cheapest_killing_check: Check whether the article has any supplementary file or accession at all - it has none, which kills it in one step.

verdict_reason: This is a Perspective article: a 25-author synthesis of a 2024 National Heart, Lung and Blood Institute workshop giving ethical and operational guidance on returning secondary genomic findings to cohort participants. It reports no measurements and deposits no data. Europe PMC records no supplementary files, no accessions and no PubMed Central copy, and a DOI search of Zenodo and Dryad found nothing. Part A1 fails because there is nothing to download, and A2, A3 and A5 fail consequently. Nothing here can support a machine learning project.
